section_summary.extract_value: This abstract reports a single study of 509 community men in London, United Kingdom, examining links between the Big Five personality traits and body image (drive for muscularity and body appreciation). Regression analyses (controlling for BMI and subjective social status) found Neuroticism positively predicted drive for muscularity and negatively predicted body appreciation, while Extraversion positively predicted body appreciation.
section_summary.evidence_source: A total of 509 men from the community in London, UK, completed measures of drive for muscularity, body appreciation, the Big Five domains, and subjective social status, and provided their demographic details. The results of a hierarchical regression showed that, once the effects of participant body mass index (BMI) and subjective social status had been accounted for, men's drive for muscularity was significantly predicted by Neuroticism (ˇ = .29). In addition, taking into account the effects of BMI and subjective social status, men's body appreciation was significantly predicted by Neuroticism (ˇ = −.35) and Extraversion (ˇ = .12).
